## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe accesses item embeddings and sequence features through a model-compatible view; `view.model` is the actual trained network. Item embeddings support the collapse check, while `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)` support ranking checks.

The supplied code does not include the BERT4Rec backbone or predictor, so it cannot establish how sequence representations are computed or verify final-nonpadding readout and appended-mask inference. The margin probe uses features at each valid target position rather than explicitly selecting a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view, device, `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`; the latter two are unused by these probes. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` performs both checks.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; stacked positive/negative IDs are scored together. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. Ranking checks run in evaluation mode without gradients.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, excluding padding and reserved mask tokens. It normalizes vectors, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result using `(mean_cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values suggest directional collapse; approximately orthogonal embeddings score 0.5.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower-tail positive-minus-negative logits across valid positions in at most ten batches. Larger margins indicate stronger sampled separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction with margin below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction with margin below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts positive and negative item categories in weak-margin and wrong-rank cases, retaining the top 20 category counts per group.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking intervention, ablation, or sensitivity test is implemented. Sampling embeddings and comparing supplied negatives are the only sampling-based checks.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The raw result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These are training-sample diagnostics, not validation HR@10 or generalization measurements. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists should be empty. Empty margin samples produce zeros, which can misleadingly appear healthy. The probes do not verify target leakage, inference consistency, representation rank, or recommendation diversity.

BERT4Rec’s bidirectional attention requires masked-item supervision: ordinary shifted next-item targets can remain visible elsewhere in the input. Deployment appends a reserved [MASK] token and scores its representation; the paper also includes last-item masking during training to match this task. Diagnostics must distinguish random interior reconstruction from prefix-only next-item prediction. [Original paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690).

Practical probes inferred from this contract: trace each supervised position to its original target, verify its required masking, and detect shifted-target exposure by position/provenance rather than banning legitimate repeated item IDs. Compare diagnostic and deployed predictor logits on identical histories, truncation, position IDs, appended masks and candidates, with dropout disabled. For left-padded inputs, select the greatest nonpadding index—including the appended mask—never nonpadding-count minus one. Test short, full-length and empty histories; full-length histories must reserve room for the mask. Deliberately expose a shifted target, omit the appended mask, and substitute count-minus-one readout as positive controls: structural checks should flag each corruption, without requiring a predictable accuracy change. Verify bidirectional attention among valid tokens and padding exclusion. Check checkpoint-reloaded predictor scores against the trained model. Report sample counts, metric definitions and unavailable/NaN results when no eligible samples exist; missing evidence must not become a healthy zero. These are proposed engineering checks, not measured findings or a diagnostic suite prescribed by the paper.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe accesses item embeddings and sequence features through a model-compatible view; `view.model` is the actual trained network. Item embeddings support the collapse check, while `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)` support ranking checks.

The supplied code does not include the BERT4Rec backbone or predictor, so it cannot establish how sequence representations are computed or verify final-nonpadding readout and appended-mask inference. The margin probe uses features at each valid target position rather than explicitly selecting a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view, device, `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`; the latter two are unused by these probes. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` performs both checks.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; stacked positive/negative IDs are scored together. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. Ranking checks run in evaluation mode without gradients.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, excluding padding and reserved mask tokens. It normalizes vectors, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result using `(mean_cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values suggest directional collapse; approximately orthogonal embeddings score 0.5.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower-tail positive-minus-negative logits across valid positions in at most ten batches. Larger margins indicate stronger sampled separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction with margin below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction with margin below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts positive and negative item categories in weak-margin and wrong-rank cases, retaining the top 20 category counts per group.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking intervention, ablation, or sensitivity test is implemented. Sampling embeddings and comparing supplied negatives are the only sampling-based checks.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The raw result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These are training-sample diagnostics, not validation HR@10 or generalization measurements. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists should be empty. Empty margin samples produce zeros, which can misleadingly appear healthy. The probes do not verify target leakage, inference consistency, representation rank, or recommendation diversity.
